docs.title: Enterprise AI Analytics Platform for Financial Services
docs.text:
Welcome to the technical documentation for the Enterprise AI Analytics Platform for Financial Services.

This platform is a modular, production-grade financial analytics and AI system designed to demonstrate enterprise-level engineering standards across:

  • Analytics Engineering: Kimball dimensional modeling, dbt Core transformations, deterministic metric definitions, and semantic layer testing.
  • Data Engineering: Multi-tier synthetic banking data generation, idempotent ingestion pipelines, and orchestrated workflows.
  • AI Engineering: LangGraph multi-agent orchestration, AST SQL parsing via SQLGlot, policy RAG retrieval, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool exposure.
  • Data Product Engineering: Typed FastAPI REST/SSE backends and interactive Streamlit executive interfaces.
  • Software Engineering & DevOps: Strict linting/formatting via Ruff, reproducible virtual environments with uv, containerized local infrastructure, and automated GitHub Actions CI/CD.

docs.title: Business Domain & Problem Statement
docs.text:
Financial institutions (commercial banks, fintechs, and payment gateways) require precise, governed insights into customer economics without risking metric hallucination or security breaches:

  1. Customer & Account Profitability: Tracking Net Interest Margin (NIM), direct operational servicing costs, and Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC).
  2. Transaction Fees & Billing Leakage: Identifying fee waiver exceptions, interchange fee variances, and wire/ACH margin capture.
  3. Contractual Pricing Compliance: Auditing realized transaction fees against contracted pricing tiers and customer volume commitments.
  4. Operational Performance: Tracking dispute resolution turnaround times, SLA compliance, and transaction failure rates.

docs.title: Architectural Principles
docs.text:
1. Deterministic Analytics over LLM Guesswork: The LLM is never the source of truth for calculations. Calculations are governed in dbt dimensional marts and validated through AST query bounds.
  2. Strict Financial Precision: Authoritative financial calculations must never use IEEE-754 floating-point arithmetic. All monetary values are enforced as DECIMAL(18, 4).
  3. Memory & Resource Efficiency: Architected to run smoothly on a 16GB RAM Mac using lightweight Docker containers (<512MB RAM) and serverless cloud tiers (free-for.dev).
  4. Defense in Depth: Text-to-SQL generation is treated as a security boundary: read-only database roles, SELECT-only AST parsing, mandatory date partitions, and timeout enforcement.

docs.title: ADR 001: Monorepo Structure, uv Package Manager, and Baseline Infrastructure
docs.text:
• Status: Approved
  • Date: 2026-11-10
  • Deciders: Lead Architect, Lead Data Engineer, Lead AI Engineer

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We are building an enterprise-grade Analytics and AI Platform for Financial Services. The development machine is a Mac with 16GB RAM. We need a modular, maintainable, and high-performance repository foundation that supports analytics engineering (dbt), data engineering (pipelines), AI engineering (LangGraph, SQLGlot), and presentation (FastAPI, Streamlit) without resource contention or tooling friction.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Modular Monorepo Structure: Adopt a single monorepo with distinct packages (packages/shared, packages/data_platform, packages/ai_services, packages/data_apps). Business logic remains decoupled from presentation and infrastructure.
  2. Unified Package Management via uv: Use Astral's uv for Python 3.12 environment management and dependency resolution. uv provides sub-second installs, deterministic lockfiles (uv.lock), and low memory usage.
  3. Primary Development Database: PostgreSQL 16 running via Docker Compose, constrained to 512MB RAM and 1 CPU. DuckDB is adopted for zero-daemon in-memory analytical unit testing.
  4. Code Quality Baseline: Use ruff for all Python linting and formatting. Use pre-commit hooks for secrets detection and file hygiene.
  5. Continuous Documentation & Hosting: Use mkdocs with mkdocs-material for continuous documentation generation, local hosting (uv run mkdocs serve), and automated publishing via GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
  • Sub-second virtual environment synchronization.
  • Zero RAM bloat on macOS (Postgres uses ~60MB idle; no persistent heavy JVM or Kafka daemons).
  • Deterministic CI checks with sub-minute execution times.
  • Interactive, searchable technical documentation updated after every milestone.
  • Negative / Constraints:
  • Developers must use uv run <tool> or activate .venv.
  • Docker Desktop must have memory allocation bounded to 6GB max.

docs.title: AI Analytics Architecture — LangGraph & Governed Q&A
1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
The AI Financial Analytics engine in packages/ai_services implements a controlled, stateful question-answering workflow powered by LangGraph. It translates natural language financial inquiries from commercial banking leadership into audited, read-only SQL queries executed against certified PostgreSQL dimensional warehouse marts.

Unlike naive text-to-SQL agents that query raw schemas or hallucinatively formulate ad-hoc calculations, this architecture enforces:

  1. Strict Metadata Resolution: All questions map to pre-approved metrics from MetadataService and formulas defined in the governed data catalog.
  2. Deterministic AST Validation: Generated SQL is parsed and inspected via SQLGlot before reaching the database, rejecting non-SELECT commands, unapproved schemas, and sensitive columns.
  3. Database-Level Least Privilege: Query execution occurs strictly under a dedicated PostgreSQL role analytics_reader with SELECT-only grants on schema analytics and a 5,000ms statement timeout.
  4. Transparent Evidence: Responses package the executive narrative together with raw records, tabular projections, reporting currency (EUR), and query latency.

docs.title: 2. LangGraph State Machine Architecture
docs.text:
The workflow is modeled as a compiled directed acyclic graph (DAG) with state-dependent conditional routing.

flowchart TD
    START([User Inquiry]) --> U[understand_question]

    U -->|Out-of-Scope / Prompt Injection| SYN[synthesize_answer]
    U -->|In-Scope Financial Query| M[resolve_metric]

    M --> R[retrieve_metadata]
    R --> G[generate_sql]
    G --> V[validate_sql]

    V -->|AST Validation Failure| SYN
    V -->|AST Security Passed| E[execute_sql]

    E --> RV[validate_results]
    RV --> SYN
    SYN --> END([Executive Response Package])

docs.title: State Schema (AIAnalyticsState)
docs.text:
The state dictionary propagates immutable contracts across node invocations:

class AIAnalyticsState(TypedDict, total=False):
    question: str
    environment: str
    conversation_id: str | None
    understanding: QuestionUnderstanding | None
    metric: MetricResolution | None
    query_context: dict[str, Any] | None
    generated_sql: str | None
    validation: SQLValidationResult | None
    query_result: QueryResult | None
    final_response: AnalyticsQueryResponse | None
    error: str | None

docs.title: 3. Workflow Nodes
docs.text: Node Name Module Path Purpose understand_question graph.nodes.question_understanding Deconstructs user input into structured intent, time periods, customer entities, and detects adversarial prompt injection attempts. resolve_metric graph.nodes.metric_resolution Matches question against MetadataService.list_metrics(), binding to governed formulas (fct_customer_revenue, fct_transactions, fct_fee_assessments). retrieve_metadata graph.nodes.metadata_retrieval Pulls approved column schemas, data types, descriptions, and joinable dimensions (dim_customers) using build_ai_query_context(). generate_sql graph.nodes.sql_generation Prompts the configured LLM provider to produce PostgreSQL 16 SELECT queries referencing certified marts. validate_sql graph.nodes.sql_validation Applies SQLGlotASTValidator to assert single-statement SELECT, allowlist conformance, and injects LIMIT 1000. execute_sql graph.nodes.sql_execution Dispatches validated query via SQLExecutionEngine connecting as analytics_reader with 5000ms timeout. validate_results graph.nodes.result_validation Inspects database return payload, formatting tabular column mappings and catching empty result sets. synthesize_answer graph.nodes.answer_synthesis Produces an executive-ready financial narrative citing figures, reporting period, currency, and audit limitations.

docs.title: 4. Conditional Branching & Security Fast-Paths
docs.text:
The LangGraph engine avoids unnecessary model invocations or database connections through two conditional edge gates:

  1. route_after_understanding:
  2. Evaluates understanding.is_out_of_scope.

  3. If user asks general non-banking queries (weather, recipes) or attempts adversarial prompt injections, the graph bypasses metric lookup, metadata retrieval, SQL generation, and database execution entirely, routing directly to synthesize_answer.

  4. route_after_validation:

  5. Evaluates validation.is_valid.
  6. If SQL parsing detects multiple statements, DDL/DML tokens, unauthorized table traversals (e.g. raw.* or metadata.*), or RESTRICTED security columns, execution is aborted immediately and routed to synthesize_answer with a detailed security explanation.

docs.title: 5. Technology Separation
docs.text: In accordance with AGENTS.md: - Business calculation logic remains strictly inside dbt models and governed metric definitions. - The LLM acts solely as a semantic parser, query generator, and synthesizer. - Database access is physically restricted at the PostgreSQL role level.

docs.title: Apache Airflow Orchestration Architecture
docs.text: This document describes the design, deployment topology, and execution architecture of the Apache Airflow data pipeline orchestration layer implemented in Phase 3 of the Financial Services Analytics & AI Platform.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Purpose & Scope
docs.text:
In Phases 1 and 2, the platform established a synthetic banking data generation engine, PostgreSQL ingestion pipeline, and a 26-model dbt dimensional warehouse. While these components could be triggered manually via CLI scripts, production financial data platforms require:

  1. Automated, Scheduled Cadence: Regular execution aligned with financial reporting periods.
  2. Deterministic Task Dependencies: Strict topological execution ensuring upstream models and data quality gates finish before analytical marts or exports run.
  3. Robust Fault Tolerance & Retries: Automated transient failure recovery, execution timeouts, and failure alerts.
  4. Governed Metadata & Lineage Tracking: Comprehensive execution telemetry, audit logs, and status dashboards.
  5. Strict Database Isolation: Complete separation between development data (analytics_platform), automated test execution (analytics_platform_test), and workflow engine state (airflow_metadata).

docs.text:
The orchestration stack runs locally via Docker Compose, optimized to run comfortably within a 16GB RAM developer environment without heavyweight distributed queues (e.g., Celery, Redis, or Kafka).

docs.title: 3. Database Isolation Strategy
docs.text:
A core tenet of the platform architecture is strict isolation across database domains:

  1. Airflow Metadata Database (airflow_metadata):
  2. Stores Airflow internal operational state: DAG run history, task instances, XCom key-value pairs, user credentials, and session locks.

  3. Completely separate from banking tables. Airflow never writes internal tables to analytics_platform or analytics_platform_test.

  4. Development Data Warehouse (analytics_platform):

  5. Hosts the raw banking tables (50 customers, 5,000 transactions, 8,289 journals, 19,053 ledger entries) and analytics dimensional star schema models.

  6. Guarded by pre-flight checks: any pipeline attempting to run against the wrong database is immediately halted.

  7. Integration Test Sandbox (analytics_platform_test):

  8. Dedicated database reserved exclusively for integration test suites (pytest) and automated test DAGs.
  9. Prevents automated tests from polluting or mutating development showcase data.

docs.title: 4. Governed DAG Pipelines
docs.text: The platform defines two production-grade DAGs in airflow/dags/:

docs.title: A. DEV Daily Analytics Pipeline (financial_analytics_dev_pipeline)
docs.text:
Scheduled daily (@daily, catchup=False, max_active_runs=1), this DAG manages the full data lifecycle:

flowchart LR
    A["1. validate_preflight<br/>Target DB guard & schemas"] --> B["2. ingest_dev_dataset<br/>Idempotent ON CONFLICT merge"]
    B --> C["3. dbt_build_analytics<br/>26 models + 462 data tests"]
    C --> D["4. reconcile_financial_integrity<br/>Double-entry & fee ceilings"]
    D --> E["5. export_sample_artifacts<br/>Public CSV dataset exports"]
    E --> F["6. log_pipeline_completion<br/>Telemetry & audit logging"]

docs.title: Task Breakdown:
docs.text:
1. validate_preflight (PythonOperator):
  2. Connects to PostgreSQL using centralized shared.config.Settings.
  3. Validates that current_database() == 'analytics_platform'. Raises AirflowException if target is incorrect.
  4. Ensures raw and analytics schemas exist.

  5. Generates environment-variable-driven dbt profile at /tmp/dbt_profiles/profiles.yml.

  6. ingest_dev_dataset (PythonOperator):

  7. Generates deterministic synthetic records using SyntheticDataGenerator(profile="DEV", seed=42).
  8. Stages and merges records using PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING logic.

  9. Zero row duplication: repeated executions leave row counts exactly unchanged.

  10. dbt_build_analytics (BashOperator):

  11. Invokes dbt build --profiles-dir /tmp/dbt_profiles --target dev.

  12. Compiles and materializes 26 models (12 staging, 5 intermediate, 9 marts) and executes 462 automated generic and singular data quality tests.

  13. reconcile_financial_integrity (PythonOperator):

  14. Executes DataReconciler verifying core accounting invariants:

    • Double-entry journal balance per currency leg (leg_diff = 0.0000).
    • Absence of ledger postings for unsettled transactions (FAILED / PENDING).
    • Referential integrity across customers, accounts, transactions, and ledger entries.
    • Mathematical fee decomposition (gross = waived + net).
    • Cumulative collection ceiling enforcement (collected <= net collectible).

  15. export_sample_artifacts (PythonOperator):

  16. Invokes export_all_samples() writing 12 raw entity CSVs and 4 analytical marts to sample_data/.

  17. log_pipeline_completion (PythonOperator):

  18. Pulls XCom metadata from upstream tasks and outputs structured audit log with execution timing and record counts.

docs.title: B. Isolated Test Pipeline (financial_analytics_test_pipeline)
docs.text:
Triggered on demand or via CI (schedule_interval=None), this DAG runs the entire pipeline end-to-end against analytics_platform_test:

flowchart LR
    T1["validate_test_preflight<br/>Verify analytics_platform_test"] --> T2["ingest_test_dataset<br/>TEST profile (10 cust, 200 txns)"]
    T2 --> T3["dbt_build_test_analytics<br/>dbt build --target test"]
    T3 --> T4["reconcile_test_integrity<br/>Full accounting audit"]

docs.title: 5. Reliability & Security Controls
docs.text:
1. No External Network Dependency:
  2. Airflow runs entirely locally in Docker with zero external API requirements.
  3. Explicit User & Host Binding:
  4. Airflow webserver binds strictly to 127.0.0.1:8080, preventing unauthorized LAN exposure.
  5. Execution Timeouts:
  6. Default timeout of 15 minutes prevents runaway hanging processes.
  7. Retry Policies:
  8. Transient failures trigger up to 2 automated retries with a 1-minute exponential backoff.
  9. Zero Hardcoded Secrets:
  10. Fernet encryption keys and database connection strings are passed exclusively through environment variables.

docs.title: 2.1 Pydantic Data Contracts
docs.text:
Every API endpoint is governed by explicit Pydantic V2 models defined in packages/ai_services/src/ai_services/schemas.py:

  • FinancialOverviewResponse: 17 typed fields including net recognized revenue, gross assessed fees, fee waivers, cash collections, uncollected arrears, pass-through costs, and realization rates.
  • RevenueTrendsResponse: Timeseries array of monthly revenue, assessed fees, and cash receipts with YYYY-MM keys.
  • CustomerRankingsResponse: Customer-level performance records with revenue, fee contributions, and arrears.
  • BillingArrearsResponse: Itemized exceptions with native and EUR-equivalent amounts, customer IDs, and fee categories.
  • AnalyticsQueryRequest / AnalyticsQueryResponse: Request validation enforcing length constraints ($3 \le \text{length} \le 500$), target environment selection (dev vs test), and returning full SQL execution traces.

docs.title: 2.2 Security & Least Privilege Enforcement
docs.text: All application-level database queries execute under the dedicated PostgreSQL role analytics_reader: * Zero DDL/DML: Insert, update, delete, truncate, drop, and create are blocked at the database engine level. * Schema Confinement: Access is revoked from PUBLIC, raw, and metadata. Access is strictly limited to 6 dimensional marts in analytics: 1. dim_accounts 2. dim_customers 3. fct_customer_revenue 4. fct_fee_assessments 5. fct_fee_collections 6. fct_transactions * Statement Timeouts: Forced 5,000ms query cancellation prevents runaway queries.

docs.title: Architecture: End-to-End Data Lineage & Dependency Graphs
1. Overview & Lineage Strategy
docs.text:
Data lineage provides complete transparency into the origin, movement, and transformation of financial records as they travel from raw synthetic banking tables to Kimball-style analytical marts.

The platform implements two complementary levels of data lineage: 1. Model-Level Lineage (Deterministic DAG): Derived directly from the compiled dbt dependency graph (parent_map and child_map in manifest.json). Guarantees 100% accuracy of inter-model dependencies. 2. Column-Level Lineage (Conservative AST Analysis): Parsed from SQL queries using sqlglot. Conservative analysis extracts direct column projections and tracks simple arithmetic/case statements, while explicitly tagging ambiguous or windowed expressions as AMBIGUOUS_COMPLEX_EXPRESSION rather than fabricating speculative column ancestry.

docs.title: 3. Lineage Engine API & Traversal Methods
docs.text: The LineageEngine class in packages/data_platform/src/data_platform/metadata/lineage.py provides bidirectional traversal capabilities:

docs.title: 3.1 Trace Mart to Raw Sources (trace_mart_to_sources)
docs.text:
Given a business mart (e.g. fct_customer_revenue), traverses upstream through intermediate and staging models to discover all underlying raw sources: 

engine = LineageEngine(parent_map=manifest_parser.parent_map)
sources = engine.trace_mart_to_sources("model.dbt_analytics.fct_customer_revenue")
# Returns:
# [
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.accounts',
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.customers',
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.fee_assessments',
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.fee_collections',
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.fx_rates',
#   'source.dbt_analytics.raw.revenue_recognitions'
# ]

docs.title: 3.2 Trace Source to Downstream Marts (trace_source_to_marts)
docs.text:
Given a raw source table (e.g. raw.fee_assessments), traverses downstream to determine which dimensional marts will be affected by schema changes or upstream data anomalies: 

marts = engine.trace_source_to_marts("source.dbt_analytics.raw.fee_assessments")
# Returns:
# [
#   'model.dbt_analytics.fct_customer_revenue',
#   'model.dbt_analytics.fct_fee_assessments',
#   'model.dbt_analytics.fct_fee_collections'

docs.title: 4. Column-Level Lineage with SQLGlot
docs.text: The ColumnLineageAnalyzer uses SQLGlot's AST visitor to extract conservative column-to-column dependencies from model queries.

docs.title: Rules:
docs.text:
1. Direct Projection: SELECT c.customer_id AS id -> id: ["customer_id"].
  2. Explicit Casts: SELECT CAST(amount AS numeric(18,4)) AS txn_amt -> txn_amt: ["amount"].
  3. Multi-Column Arithmetic: SELECT gross_amount - waived_amount AS net_amount -> net_amount: ["gross_amount", "waived_amount"].
  4. Ambiguous Window / Aggregation: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER (...) -> mapped only to contained column identifiers without fabricating upstream columns.
  5. Jinja Pre-Processing: Strips {{ ref(...) }} and {{ source(...) }} macros to valid SQL table aliases before AST parsing, avoiding unparseable syntax errors.

docs.title: High-Throughput PostgreSQL Batch Ingestion
docs.text: This document details the architecture and operational mechanics of the synthetic data ingestion pipeline powering the Enterprise AI Analytics Platform.

docs.title: 1. End-to-End Pipeline Workflow
docs.text:
The ingestion pipeline decouples memory-intensive synthetic banking generation from relational persistence using unlogged staging tables, binary-efficient streaming COPY, and atomic transactional merges:

flowchart TD

        A["SyntheticDataGenerator (seed=42)"] --> B["CustomerEngine & AccountEngine"]
        A --> C["FXEngine (ECB Triangulated Matrix)"]
        A --> D["TransactionEngine (Commercial Flows)"]
        D --> E["LedgerEngine (Double-Entry Journals)"]
        D --> F["FeeEngine (Assessments & Sweeps)"]
    end

    subgraph StagingPhase["2. Staged Bulk COPY (psycopg 3)"]
        G["Unlogged Staging Tables (staging.*)"]
        B & C & D & E & F -->|Bulk Stream via COPY| G
    end

    subgraph MergePhase["3. Atomic Transactional Merge"]
        G -->|INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING| H[("PostgreSQL Raw Tables (raw.*)")]
        I["Audit Manifest Logging"] --> H
    end

    subgraph AuditPhase["4. Data Quality & Reconciliation"]
        H --> J{"DataReconciler Audit"}
        J -->|Check 1| K["Double-Entry Balanced per Currency Leg"]
        J -->|Check 2| L["Zero Postings on Unsettled Txns"]
        J -->|Check 3| M["Referential Integrity (No Orphans)"]
        J -->|Check 4| N["Fee Math & Collection Ceilings"]
        J -->|Check 5| O["Currency Domains (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF)"]
        K & L & M & N & O -->|All 7 Checks Passed| P["Batch Marked COMPLETED"]
        J -->|Any Check Fails| Q["Rollback Transaction & Alert"]
    end

docs.title: A. Unlogged Staging Tables
docs.text: To achieve multi-thousand row-per-second ingestion without saturating disk I/O on development machines (16GB RAM Mac), the pipeline loads records into PostgreSQL UNLOGGED tables in the staging schema. Unlogged tables bypass Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) during the copy phase.

docs.title: B. Streaming COPY Protocol
docs.text:
Rather than generating thousands of parameterized INSERT statements, the pipeline uses psycopg 3 COPY streams: 

with cur.copy("COPY staging.transactions FROM STDIN") as copy:
    for t in data.transactions:
        copy.write_row(...)

docs.title: C. Idempotent Transactional Merge
docs.text: Once all tables are staged, the pipeline merges records into raw.* tables within a single database transaction using ON CONFLICT (pk) DO NOTHING. This ensures: - Safe rerunability on duplicate executions. - Zero duplicate records created on retries. - Foreign key constraints are enforced atomically. - Failures result in complete rollback, leaving no partial batches.

docs.title: 2.1 Artifact Publishing & Snapshot Versioning (DbtArtifactManager)
docs.text: When dbt build and dbt docs generate complete: 1. DbtArtifactManager validates that manifest.json, catalog.json, and run_results.json exist and contain non-empty top-level keys. 2. A timestamped and UUID-tagged snapshot directory is created at artifacts/dbt/<target>/<run_id>/. 3. If build status is SUCCESS, the snapshot is atomically promoted to artifacts/dbt/<target>/latest/. 4. Artifact telemetry (model count, test count, dbt version, schema) is compiled into an ArtifactRun record.

docs.title: 2.2 Semantic Extraction & Synthesis
docs.text:
• DbtManifestParser: Reads models, sources, seeds, and test nodes. Extracts column descriptions, model tags, grains, foreign key relationships, and adjacency parent/child dependency maps.
  • DbtCatalogParser: Inspects physical PostgreSQL information schema types (e.g. numeric(18,4), character varying(64), timestamp with time zone) and ordinal positions, merging them with logical column metadata.
  • ClassificationEngine: Applies enterprise sensitivity rules, mapping columns to CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED, or INTERNAL based on naming heuristics and YAML meta tags.
  • LineageEngine: Constructs directed graph edges (LineageEdge) across models, sources, and columns.
  • MetricRegistry & MetricValidator: Ingests governed financial metrics, verifying that referenced models, columns, and SQL expressions are valid.

docs.text:

docs.title: 4. Governed Security Boundary: Queryable Model Allowlist
docs.text: To eliminate hallucinations and prevent AI agents from generating SQL against uncurated staging tables or raw tables, the MetadataService enforces a strict allowlist:

docs.title: 4.1 Permitted Models
docs.text:
• dim_customers: Customer master dimension.
  • dim_accounts: Bank account holdings and subledger balances.
  • dim_gl_accounts: General Ledger Chart of Accounts.
  • dim_date: Enterprise calendar date dimension.
  • fct_transactions: Commercial payments and payment rails.
  • fct_fee_assessments: Contractual fee assessments, waivers, and net collectible amounts.
  • fct_fee_collections: Collection attempts, sweep execution, and cash realization.
  • fct_customer_revenue: Monthly customer fee profitability and revenue recognition.
  • fct_ledger_entries: Double-entry general ledger postings.

docs.title: 4.2 Prohibited Models
docs.text:
• Raw sources (raw.*): Direct raw tables lack dimensional joins and business definitions.
  • Staging models (stg_*): Transient 1-to-1 cleanses.
  • Intermediate models (int_*): Non-surfaced multi-table business joins.

If an AI agent requests context for stg_transactions or raw.transactions, MetadataService.build_ai_query_context() immediately raises PermissionError and halts execution.

docs.title: 1. Security Philosophy
docs.text:
In the Financial Services Analytics & AI Platform, the AI query execution boundary is treated as an adversarial perimeter. Large Language Models must never be granted unconstrained database access or relied upon to self-police query safety through prompt instructions.

Security is implemented in depth through three independent defensive perimeters:

[ Natural Language Input ]
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Perimeter 1: Intent & Prompt Injection Shield                │
│ (Rejects system overrides, SQL drop/delete directives)      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │ (Sanitized inquiry)
           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Perimeter 2: SQLGlot AST Semantic & Boundary Validator     │
│ - Single statement enforcement (rejects stacked semicolons) │
│ - Pure SELECT root only (rejects INSERT, UPDATE, DDL)       │
│ - Strict Schema & Mart Allowlist (schema 'analytics' only)  │
│ - RESTRICTED Column Pattern Scanning (password, secrets)    │
│ - Row Limit Clamping (enforces LIMIT 1000)                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │ (Sanitized, clamped SQL)
           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Perimeter 3: PostgreSQL Database Role & Session Sandbox     │
│ - Role: analytics_reader (SELECT-only on analytics.*)       │
│ - Revoked: raw.*, staging.*, metadata.*, intermediate.*     │
│ - Session timeout: SET statement_timeout = '5000ms'         │
│ - autocommit=True, read-only transaction semantics          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │
           ▼
[ Analytics Mart Tables ]

docs.title: 2. Perimeter 1: Prompt Injection Shield
docs.text:
When incoming questions are processed by QuestionUnderstanding, the system tests for known adversarial prompt injection vectors: - System prompt overrides ("Ignore previous instructions", "System override:") - Destructive directives ("drop table", "delete from", "truncate") - Schema traversal hints ("SELECT * FROM raw.", "information_schema") - Secret credential exfiltration ("password", "api_key", "secret tokens")

If detected, is_out_of_scope is flagged, causing immediate routing to narrative rejection without constructing database prompts.

docs.title: 3. Perimeter 2: SQLGlot AST Validator
docs.text:
The AST validator inspects the compiled query representation using SQLGlot under the postgres dialect before physical execution:

validator = SQLGlotASTValidator(dialect="postgres", max_limit=1000)
result = validator.validate_and_sanitize(generated_sql)

docs.title: AST Enforcement Rules
docs.text:
1. Single Statement Integrity: Semicolon-delimited compound queries (SELECT ...; DROP TABLE ...;) generate multiple AST expression roots. Any query yielding len(expressions) > 1 is immediately rejected.
  2. Forbidden Expressions: Trees containing exp.Insert, exp.Update, exp.Delete, exp.Create, exp.Drop, exp.Alter, exp.TruncateTable, exp.Command, or exp.Pragma are blocked.
  3. Root Expression Validation: The top-level AST root must evaluate strictly to exp.Select.
  4. Schema Allowlist:
  5. Permitted: analytics or empty (auto-normalized to analytics).
  6. Disallowed: raw, staging, intermediate, metadata, public, information_schema, pg_catalog.
  7. Table Allowlist:
  8. Queries can only touch tables defined in QUERYABLE_ALLOWLIST:
    • dim_accounts, dim_customers, fct_customer_revenue, fct_fee_assessments, fct_journal_entries, fct_transactions.
  9. Restricted Column Redaction:
  10. Column identifiers matching sensitive terms (password, secret, api_key, token, private_key, credential) trigger rejection.
  11. Deterministic Row Clamping:
  12. If no LIMIT clause exists, LIMIT 1000 is appended.
  13. If a LIMIT clause requests more than 1,000 rows (e.g. LIMIT 50000), it is clamped to 1000.

docs.title: 4. Perimeter 3: PostgreSQL analytics_reader Sandbox
docs.text: Even if an attacker bypassed AST parsing, the database engine enforces physical permission isolation.

docs.title: Provisioning DDL
docs.text:
Role setup is provisioned via packages/data_platform/src/data_platform/sql/provision_analytics_reader.sql:

DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'analytics_reader') THEN
        CREATE ROLE analytics_reader WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'analytics_reader_secret';
    END IF;
END $$;

ALTER ROLE analytics_reader SET statement_timeout = '5000ms';

REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM analytics_reader;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA raw FROM analytics_reader;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA staging FROM analytics_reader;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA intermediate FROM analytics_reader;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA metadata FROM analytics_reader;

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA analytics TO analytics_reader;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA analytics TO analytics_reader;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA analytics GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO analytics_reader;

docs.title: Statement Timeout Protection
docs.text: To prevent denial-of-service (DoS) via Cartesian joins or table scans, analytics_reader has a role-level and session-level statement timeout of 5000ms. If an analytical query takes longer than 5 seconds to complete, PostgreSQL forcibly terminates the backend transaction with psycopg.errors.QueryCanceled.

docs.title: Phase 1: Synthetic Financial Data Generation & Accounting Engine
Overview & Architecture
docs.text: Phase 1 provides the synthetic data generation foundation for the Enterprise AI Analytics Platform. Rather than producing superficial mock data, it implements an authoritative financial simulation enforcing double-entry general ledger bookkeeping, multi-currency foreign exchange settlement, and contractual fee billing lifecycles.

docs.title: Economic Context: Customer Sells EUR 1,000 to Receive USD
docs.text: Consider a corporate customer initiating an FX conversion: - Customer sells: 1,000.0000 EUR - Mid-market exchange rate: 1.085000 (1 EUR = 1.0850 USD) - Customer realized rate (20 bps margin): 1.082830 - Customer receives: 1,082.8300 USD - Bank realized FX spread revenue: 2.1700 USD

docs.title: Accounting Model & T-Accounts
docs.text:
The transaction generates two independently balanced single-currency legs bridged by the bank's internal foreign exchange clearing position (GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING):

flowchart TD
    subgraph Leg 1: EUR Leg
        A["Customer EUR Deposits<br/>(GL_LIAB_CUSTOMER_DEPOSITS)<br/>DEBIT 1,000.0000 EUR"]
        B["Bank FX Clearing Position<br/>(GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING)<br/>CREDIT 1,000.0000 EUR"]
        A <--> B
    end
    subgraph Leg 2: USD Leg
        C["Bank FX Clearing Position<br/>(GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING)<br/>DEBIT 1,085.0000 USD"]
        D["Customer USD Deposits<br/>(GL_LIAB_CUSTOMER_DEPOSITS)<br/>CREDIT 1,082.8300 USD"]
        E["FX Spread Revenue<br/>(GL_REV_FX_SPREAD)<br/>CREDIT 2.1700 USD"]
        C <--> D
        C <--> E
    end

docs.title: Detailed T-Account Table
docs.text: Currency Account Normal Balance Posting Type Amount Economic Interpretation EUR GL_LIAB_CUSTOMER_DEPOSITS CREDIT DEBIT 1,000.0000 Bank's EUR liability decreases (customer balance reduced) EUR GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING DEBIT CREDIT 1,000.0000 Bank receives EUR 1,000 into its open FX inventory USD GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING DEBIT DEBIT 1,085.0000 Bank delivers USD 1,085 from its open FX inventory USD GL_LIAB_CUSTOMER_DEPOSITS CREDIT CREDIT 1,082.8300 Bank's USD liability increases (customer receives USD) USD GL_REV_FX_SPREAD CREDIT CREDIT 2.1700 Bank recognizes realized trading spread revenue once

docs.title: Currency Leg Balances & Reconciliation
docs.text:
• EUR Leg Total: Debits = Credits = 1,000.0000 EUR
  • USD Leg Total: Debits = Credits = 1,085.0000 USD (1,082.8300 + 2.1700)
  • FX Spread Recognition: Realized spread is recognized exactly once in destination currency (USD) at transaction time.

docs.title: 2. Documented Accounting Assumptions & Simplifications
docs.text:
1. FX Clearing Position: GL_ASSET_FX_CLEARING functions as an open multi-currency suspense and position account. Across conversions, it accumulates per-currency debit and credit balances representing the bank's net open currency exposure.
  2. Card Settlement Clearing: Card transactions clear through GL_ASSET_CENTRAL_BANK as a generalized settlement rail, avoiding unnecessary card scheme clearing complexity before dbt modelling.
  3. Two-Way Payment Directionality: Wire transfers and ACH payments support both outbound customer payments (DEBIT) and inbound customer receipts (CREDIT), while card settlements and FX conversions represent customer outbound flows (DEBIT).
  4. Append-Only Reversals: Full and partial reversals generate explicit new reverse journals referencing the original posting ID with cumulative ceiling protection (max 100%).

docs.title: 3. M1.4: Fee Assessment & Collection Engine
docs.text: The Fee Engine (FeeEngine) decouples fee assessment from collection execution to model real-world banking operations.

docs.title: Fee Lifecycle States
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2

    ASSESSED --> PARTIALLY_WAIVED: Contractual Discount / Promo
    ASSESSED --> WAIVED_IN_FULL: 100% Waiver Granted
    ASSESSED --> FAILED: Insufficient Funds / Account Frozen
    ASSESSED --> PARTIAL: Partial Balance Sweep
    PARTIAL --> SETTLED: Subsequent Sweep
    ASSESSED --> SETTLED: Full Balance Sweep
    SETTLED --> REVERSED: Fee Dispute / Refund

docs.title: Governing Pricing Schedules
docs.text: Standard governed base fees and variable basis points per transaction type and customer segment: - Institutional Wire: 15.00 EUR flat + 5 bps (0.0005) - Commercial SME Wire: 10.00 EUR flat + 10 bps (0.0010) - Retail Wealth Wire: 5.00 EUR flat + 15 bps (0.0015) - Standard SEPA ACH: 0.50 EUR flat - Card Merchant Interchange: 0.20 EUR flat + 120 bps (0.0120)

docs.title: Double-Entry Accounting for Collected Fees
docs.text: When a fee collection succeeds: - DEBIT: GL_LIAB_CUSTOMER_DEPOSITS (Customer balance decreases) - CREDIT: Appropriate fee revenue account (GL_REV_WIRE_FEES, GL_REV_ACH_FEES, GL_REV_CARD_FEES, GL_REV_FX_SPREAD) - Pass-Through Expense: External clearing costs are logged in RevenueRecognitionRecord and netted against gross collections to compute net recognized revenue.

docs.title: 4. M1.5: PostgreSQL Raw Schema & Staging Pipeline
docs.text:
The ingestion pipeline delivers high-throughput, idempotent ingestion from Python into PostgreSQL 16 using unlogged staging tables, binary-efficient COPY streaming, and transactional SQL merges.

flowchart LR

    B -->|Validate Constraints| C[Transactional SQL Merge]
    C -->|Idempotent ON CONFLICT| D[PostgreSQL Raw Tables]
    D -->|Post-Load Quality Audit| E[Data Reconciler]
    E -->|7 Invariants Verified| F[Ingestion Batch Manifest]

docs.title: PostgreSQL Raw Tables Architecture
docs.text:
All financial tables use NUMERIC(18, 4) for monetary amounts, NUMERIC(18, 6) for exchange rates, and NUMERIC(7, 4) for interest rates:

  1. raw.gl_accounts: Master chart of accounts (14 standard bank GL accounts).
  2. raw.customers: Customer profiles across Institutional, Commercial SME, and Retail Wealth.
  3. raw.accounts: Multi-currency customer bank accounts subledger.
  4. raw.overdraft_facilities: Credit agreements and penalty rate terms.
  5. raw.fx_rates: Historical daily triangulated ECB cross-rate matrix.
  6. raw.transactions: Commercial payment, wire, card, and FX operations.
  7. raw.journals: Double-entry accounting journal events grouping balanced legs.
  8. raw.ledger_entries: Append-only debit/credit ledger postings.
  9. raw.fee_assessments: Contractual pricing evaluations and fee waivers.
  10. raw.fee_collections: Collection execution sweeps and failure tracking.
  11. raw.revenue_recognitions: Net recognized revenue after pass-through costs.
  12. raw.ingestion_batch_manifests: Audit lineage headers tracking batches.

docs.title: Governed SQL Files
docs.text: In compliance with project engineering standards, SQL queries and schema DDL are stored in dedicated, inspectable SQL files: - schema_raw.sql: Raw table DDL, foreign keys, and indexes. - schema_staging.sql: Unlogged staging tables for fast COPY. - merge_staging_to_raw.sql: Transactional idempotent merge logic. - reconciliation.sql: Automated reconciliation queries.

docs.title: Automated Reconciliation Checks
docs.text:
Every ingested batch automatically validates 7 invariants before marking completion:

Check Name Target Table Rule & Economic Invariant DOUBLE_ENTRY_JOURNAL_BALANCING raw.ledger_entries Every journal must balance per currency leg ($\sum \text{debits} = \sum \text{credits}$). NO_POSTINGS_FOR_UNSETTLED_TXNS raw.transactions Transactions with status FAILED or PENDING must have zero ledger postings. ACCOUNT_CUSTOMER_REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY raw.accounts Every bank account must link to a valid customer record. TRANSACTION_ACCOUNT_REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY raw.transactions Every transaction must originate from a valid bank account. FEE_ASSESSMENT_DECOMPOSITION raw.fee_assessments $\text{Gross Assessed} = \text{Waived} + \text{Net Collectible}$. FEE_COLLECTION_CEILING_ENFORCEMENT raw.fee_collections $\sum \text{Collected} \le \text{Net Collectible}$ across all retry attempts. SUPPORTED_CURRENCY_DOMAINS raw.accounts Currencies must belong to approved domain (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF).

docs.title: 3. Architectural & Modelling Decisions
docs.text:
1. Strict Separation of Native vs. Reporting Currencies: Every financial model preserves the original transaction/account currency (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF) and never sums disparate currencies together. Where cross-currency reporting is needed, models join stg_fx_rates on the effective business date (to_currency = 'EUR') to compute explicit *_eur columns using NUMERIC(18, 4) arithmetic. Missing FX rates are never defaulted to 1.0 and are guarded by assert_no_missing_fx_rates_in_marts.sql.
  2. Fan-Out Prevention via Intermediate Pre-Aggregation:
  3. int_customer_accounts pre-aggregates stg_overdraft_facilities by account_id before joining to stg_accounts.
  4. int_fee_lifecycle joins stg_fee_collections to stg_revenue_recognitions at collection_id grain and pre-aggregates to assessment_id before joining to stg_fee_assessments.
  5. assert_no_customer_revenue_fanout.sql mathematically verifies that fct_customer_revenue sums match fct_fee_assessments across every currency to 0.0000 tolerance.
  6. Collection-Based Revenue Recognition: Following the Phase 1 accounting baseline, fee revenue is recognized upon successful cash collection (collection_status IN ('SETTLED', 'PARTIAL')), with direct pass-through costs and reversals deducted to arrive at net_recognized_revenue.

docs.title: 5. Known Limitations & Future Work
docs.text:
• Collection-Based Recognition: The platform uses cash-collection-based fee revenue recognition rather than multi-period IFRS 15 accrual accounting.
  • Single-Attempt Collection Simulation: In the current synthetic DEV dataset, fee collections execute a single sweep attempt (collection_attempt_number = 1). The dbt intermediate and mart models (int_fee_lifecycle, fct_fee_assessments, fct_fee_collections) are engineered to handle multi-attempt retries without fan-out.
  • Static Dimension Attributes: Customer segments and account statuses are modelled as Type 1 dimensions because the raw schema does not store historical SCD2 effective-date change logs for customer/account attributes.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
Phase 3 transitions the Financial Services Analytics & AI Platform from ad-hoc script execution to a production-grade, scheduled, and fault-tolerant orchestration architecture powered by Apache Airflow 2.10.3 on Python 3.12.

The orchestration layer coordinates the deterministic synthetic banking data generator, PostgreSQL staging and raw ingestion, 26 dbt dimensional analytics models (462 automated tests), double-entry accounting reconciliation, and public sample dataset exports.

All operations execute under strict database isolation guards, ensuring that operational workflow state (airflow_metadata), development data (analytics_platform), and integration test sandboxes (analytics_platform_test) remain strictly segregated.

docs.title: Phase 4.1 Audit: Financial Integrity, Governance & Provenance
1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This audit assesses the technical integrity, financial mathematical validity, metadata provenance, and security boundaries of the platform following the completion of Phase 3.1 and Phase 4, prior to starting Phase 5 (LangGraph-based AI Financial Analytics).

The audit identified and corrected several concrete defects in financial metric formulas, date references, and metadata snapshot promotion logic, hardened Airflow DAG execution across both environments, verified database schema nullability constraints, and established explicit security specifications for Phase 5.

docs.title: 2.1 Financial Metric Integrity & Formula Corrections
docs.text: Metric ID Audit Finding Root Cause Implemented Fix effective_take_rate Currency Mismatch in Ratio Numerator was in EUR (net_recognized_revenue_eur) while denominator was in un-converted native currency (gross_assessed_fee_amount). In multi-currency aggregations, mixing EUR with USD/GBP/CHF invalidates the ratio. Changed denominator to gross_assessed_fee_amount_eur. Renamed metric to Effective Fee Realization Rate to accurately reflect realized fee potential. fee_collection_rate Multi-Currency Aggregation Safety Summing collected_amount across differing currencies yields distorted portfolio-level ratios. Standardized ratio on audited EUR columns: SUM(collected_amount_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(net_collectible_amount_eur), 0). average_customer_daily_balance Invalid Date Field Reference Catalog referenced onboarding_date on dim_accounts, which does not exist in dim_accounts (onboarding_date belongs to dim_customers). Updated date_field to opened_date (the valid date column on dim_accounts). net_customer_profitability Profitability vs. Contribution Margin Metric was labeled "Net Customer Profitability" while actually computing Net Fee Revenue (after network pass-through costs and reversals, but before operating expenses and cost of funds). Clarified metric name as Net Customer Fee Contribution Margin (Contribution Margin I) and documented limitations. reversal_rate Count vs. Volume Ambiguity Definition did not explicitly state whether the rate was operational count or monetary throughput. Documented as Count-Based Operational Reversal Rate and detailed volume-based derivation. billing_exception_rate Arrears vs. Sweep Failures Definition required clarification regarding collection failures vs. transient arrears. Verified against warehouse: captures 200 sweep collection failures (collection_status = 'FAILED') and any partial arrears.

docs.title: 2.2 Metadata Provenance & Snapshot Reliability
docs.text:
• Defect Fixed: In MetadataRepository.save_snapshot(), an unconditional UPDATE metadata.artifact_runs SET is_latest = FALSE WHERE environment = %s was executed prior to run insertion. If a failed run (is_latest = False) was persisted, it demoted the active catalog without promoting a new one, leaving no active latest catalog.
  • Fix: Wrapped the demotion update in if run.is_latest:, ensuring failed refreshes cannot alter or demote the existing successful catalog. Added regression integration test test_failed_metadata_run_does_not_demote_latest.
  • Provenance Defect Fixed: In MetadataExtractor, database_name was hardcoded to "analytics_platform". When running against test, the run metadata recorded analytics_platform rather than analytics_platform_test.
  • Fix: Dynamically resolved database_name from parsed model metadata or target environment defaults.
  • Atomic Promotion: Confirmed that DbtArtifactManager.publish_artifacts() only copies snapshots to artifacts/dbt/<env>/latest/ when build_status == 'SUCCESS'.

docs.title: 2.3 Ingestion Reliability & Batch Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Batch Lifecycle Audit: Verified that raw.ingestion_batch_manifests records:
  • STARTED: Committed independently prior to staging copy.
  • COMPLETED: Committed atomically with the raw table merge.
  • FAILED: In exception blocks, conn.rollback() resets staging, and _record_manifest(status='FAILED') is committed independently.
  • Database Schema Verification: Inspected information_schema.columns in both live PostgreSQL databases:
  • analytics_platform.raw.ingestion_batch_manifests.completed_at: is_nullable = YES.
  • analytics_platform_test.raw.ingestion_batch_manifests.completed_at: is_nullable = YES.
  • Verified that STARTED and FAILED records (where completed_at is NULL) satisfy database constraints without constraint violations.

docs.title: 2.4 Security Readiness & Boundaries for Phase 5
docs.text:
The audit verified the distinction between Phase 4 metadata filtering and Phase 5 execution security:

[Phase 4: Semantic Filtering Layer (Implemented)]
  - MetadataService.build_ai_query_context(model_name)
    → Allowed: 9 dimensional marts (dim_customers, dim_accounts, dim_gl_accounts, dim_date,
               fct_transactions, fct_fee_assessments, fct_fee_collections,
               fct_customer_revenue, fct_ledger_entries)
    → Blocked: raw.*, stg_*, int_* (raises PermissionError)
  - RESTRICTED columns (passwords, tokens, keys) stripped from AI context

[Phase 5: Execution Boundary Security (Required Before Model Calls)]
  1. SQLGlot AST Safety Parser:
     - Disallow DDL (CREATE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE) and DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).
     - Disallow multi-statement query chaining.
     - Enforce that all exp.Table nodes belong strictly to analytics.<allowed_mart>.
  2. Database Role Isolation:
     - Dedicated read-only role (analytics_reader) granted SELECT ONLY on analytics schema.
  3. Execution Guards:
     - Statement timeout (5000ms).
     - Driver-enforced hard LIMIT 1000.

docs.title: Enterprise Financial Analytics & AI Platform: Architecture & Exploration Guide
1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
The Enterprise AI Analytics Platform for Financial Services is a modular, production-grade financial data, analytics engineering, and governed AI platform.

It solves a critical challenge in commercial banking and financial operations: bridging the gap between raw ledger transactions, governed accounting metrics, and natural-language AI inquiries without compromising financial accuracy, data contracts, or database security.

Whether you are a data engineer, financial analyst, software developer, or curious explorer, this guide walks you through the system architecture, business principles, and how to interact with the platform.

docs.title: What Does the Platform Do?
docs.text:
• Tracks Revenue & Fee Collection: Commercial banks charge transaction fees, interchange, and account servicing charges. This platform models the complete journey from initial fee assessment to waiver concession, cash settlement, arrears, and recognized net revenue.
  • Enforces Accounting Integrity: Ensures that every euro of recognized revenue reconciles to double-entry ledger entries and dimensional data models down to the exact cent.
  • Powers Natural-Language Analytics: Allows users to ask conversational questions (e.g. "What was our total net revenue?" or "Which clients have outstanding fees?") while enforcing compile-time SQL safety gates so the AI cannot hallucinate numbers or execute malicious queries.

  2. Phase 2: dbt Dimensional Analytics Engineering: Kimball-style star schema featuring 26 dbt models across staging, intermediate, and marts, validated by 462 data tests.
  3. Phase 3: Airflow Pipeline Orchestration: Production Apache Airflow 2.10.3 stack with LocalExecutor orchestrating deterministic daily ingestion, dbt builds, and financial reconciliation.

docs.title: 3.1 The Reconciled Revenue Accounting Bridge
docs.text:
The platform enforces strict accounting integrity across the commercial fee lifecycle:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Gross Assessed Fees} & = \mathbf{€467,449.70} \ - \text{Discretionary Waivers} & = - \mathbf{€8,061.56} \ \hline = \text{Net Collectible Fee Pool} & = \mathbf{€459,388.14} \ - \text{Uncollected Arrears (200 assessments)} & = - \mathbf{€29,280.10} \ \hline = \text{Cash Collected Sweeps} & = \mathbf{€430,108.04} \ - \text{Fee Reversals} & = - \mathbf{€0.00} \ - \text{Card Scheme / Clearing Pass-Through} & = - \mathbf{€21,505.40} \ \hline = \mathbf{Net Recognized Revenue} & = \mathbf{€408,602.64} \end{aligned}$$

$$\Delta_{\text{reconciliation}} = €29,280.10 + €21,505.40 = \mathbf{€50,785.50}$$

Every figure is backed by dimensional marts (analytics.fct_customer_revenue and analytics.fct_fee_assessments) and asserted in automated regression suites.

docs.title: 4. Security & Boundary Defense-in-Depth
docs.text:
The AI query layer is engineered as an untrusted boundary:

  1. AST Parsing (SQLGlot): Queries are parsed into abstract syntax trees. Statements containing DDL (DROP, ALTER, CREATE), DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), multiple statements (;), subqueries targeting non-marts, or schema escapes are rejected before execution.
  2. Database Engine Role Separation (analytics_reader):
  3. Hard statement_timeout = '5000ms'.
  4. Access revoked from PUBLIC, raw, and metadata.
  5. Explicit SELECT permissions restricted to only 6 dimensional marts.
  6. Execution Guardrails: Result sets are hard-clamped to a maximum of 1,000 rows.
  7. API Authentication & Throttling: Token bucket rate limiting (120 req/min) and Bearer/API key authentication for protected endpoints.

docs.title: 5. Technology Decision Matrix
docs.text: Layer Selected Technology Why Selected Trade-offs & Alternatives Considered Language & Tooling Python 3.12, uv Modern typing, high-speed virtual environment and lockfile resolution Poetry/Conda: uv is 10–100x faster and maintains deterministic lockfiles. Warehouse PostgreSQL 16 Relational reliability, robust role-based security, CTEs, window functions DuckDB is used for fast analytical unit tests; PostgreSQL is chosen for true multi-user concurrency and role security. Transformations dbt Core 1.8+ Industry standard for dimensional modeling, testing, and automated documentation Raw SQL scripts: lack automated testing, lineage generation, and dependency DAG execution. Orchestration Apache Airflow 2.10.3 Battle-tested task dependency management, retries, and SLA observability Prefect/Dagster: Airflow remains the enterprise benchmark in financial institutions. AI Orchestration LangGraph Deterministic state machine, explicit conditional routing, tool inspection Raw LangChain/AutoGPT: LangGraph provides precise control over validation gates. SQL Validation SQLGlot Pure Python AST parsing and dialect-aware schema normalization Regex: Regex is fragile and easily bypassed by SQL injection obfuscation. Application FastAPI + Streamlit High-throughput async REST backend paired with rapid executive presentation React frontend: Streamlit allows fast data iteration in Python while maintaining executive polish.

docs.title: 6.1 Cold-Start & Inactivity Spin-Down
docs.text:
• Symptom: On free hosting tiers (e.g., Streamlit Community Cloud or Render Free), requests may take 20–40 seconds on first load after inactivity.
  • Cause: Container suspended to save compute resources.
  • Resolution:
  • The frontend displays an automatic wake-up spinner.
  • For continuous availability without sleep states, use Railway ($5/mo) or a single-node VPS (€3.79/mo).

docs.title: 6.2 Connection Pool Saturation
docs.text:
• Symptom: OperationalError: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections.
  • Cause: Too many concurrent Streamlit threads or API workers exceeding PostgreSQL max_connections.
  • Resolution:
  • Adjust DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE=5 in .env.
  • Ensure all database connections use Python context managers (with get_postgres_reader_connection() as conn:) which automatically return connections to the pool upon completion.

docs.title: 6.3 Statement Timeout Enforcement (5000ms)
docs.text:
• Symptom: QueryCanceled: canceling statement due to statement timeout.
  • Cause: AI or user executed an unindexed or Cartesian join exceeding the 5,000ms safety threshold.
  • Resolution:
  • Expected behavior: protects the warehouse from runaway queries.
  • Ensure queries use indexed join columns (e.g., customer_id, account_id) or filter by transaction_date.

docs.title: 6.4 API Authentication Rejection (401 Unauthorized)
docs.text:
• Symptom: 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing API key.
  • Cause: Client omitted the X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer <key> header when API_AUTH_ENABLED=true.
  • Resolution:
  • Pass the key in headers: curl -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" ...
  • In development or local demonstration, set API_AUTH_ENABLED=false in .env to allow anonymous access.

The platform enforces strict database separation between development/portfolio analytics and automated integration testing:

Environment Database Name Configured Via Purpose & Safety Controls Development / Portfolio analytics_platform POSTGRES_DB=analytics_platform Default target for data_platform.ingestion.run, dbt build (--target dev), and export_samples. Protected against accidental test truncation. Automated Integration Tests analytics_platform_test POSTGRES_TEST_DB=analytics_platform_test Dedicated database used exclusively by tests/integration/. Automatically provisioned by ensure_test_database_exists() without dropping existing databases.
  • Integration Test Connection Routing: All PostgreSQL integration tests in tests/integration/ use get_test_postgres_connection(), which connects strictly to analytics_platform_test regardless of POSTGRES_DB in .env.
  • Destructive Operation Safety Guard: truncate_raw_tables() in packages/data_platform/src/data_platform/ingestion/ddl.py executes assert_is_test_database(conn) (SELECT current_database()) and raises PermissionError if called against analytics_platform or any database other than analytics_platform_test (unless explicitly invoked via the CLI --reset flag).

docs.text: In financial services, evaluating AI accuracy, hallucination prevention, and security resistance is a core governance requirement. The platform maintains a curated evaluation suite under packages/ai_services/src/ai_services/eval/ comprising 32 curated benchmark cases.

docs.title: 2. Benchmark Case Taxonomy

Category Cases Target Business Area Example Question Revenue 5 Net recognized revenue, IFRS 15 accruals, take rates "What was our total net recognized revenue?" Customers 5 Revenue ranking, customer segment contribution "Which customers generated the most revenue?" Fees 5 Fee collection rate, gross assessments, waivers "What is our overall fee collection rate?" Reversals 3 Payment cancellations, chargeback rates "What is our transaction reversal rate?" docs.title: 1. Classification Architecture
docs.text:
The platform categorizes all database assets, tables, columns, and metric outputs into four hierarchical governance sensitivity tiers:

[RESTRICTED]  -> Level 4: Passwords, tokens, API keys, private signing keys. Strictly prohibited in analytics.
     │
[CONFIDENTIAL] -> Level 3: Synthetic customer identifiers, account numbers, financial balances, amounts.
     │
 [INTERNAL]   -> Level 2: Model descriptions, metric formulas, schema lineage, platform documentation.
     │
  [PUBLIC]    -> Level 1: Public synthetic summaries, marketing descriptions, open API docs.

docs.title: 2. Sensitivity Tiers & Handling Rules
docs.text: Tier Sensitivity Level Description Handling & Masking Rules PUBLIC 1 Non-sensitive information suitable for open distribution. No restriction on display, export, or usage. INTERNAL 2 Platform definitions, metadata tags, metric schemas, and business glossaries intended for internal users. Accessible across internal services and authenticated staff. Excluded from public external outputs. CONFIDENTIAL 3 Customer identifiers, bank account holdings, transaction principal amounts, and fees. Must be protected with role-based access. Raw customer identifiers are masked or redacted in AI context summaries. RESTRICTED 4 Security credentials, database connection passwords, API signing tokens, and private keys. Strictly prohibited in warehouse tables, analytical models, dbt artifacts, and logs. Any occurrence triggers automated redaction.

docs.title: 3. Heuristic Pattern Detection & Inheritance
docs.text:
The ClassificationEngine assigns classifications through a 3-stage process:

  1. Explicit YAML Tagging: If a dbt model or column defines meta: {classification: 'CONFIDENTIAL'} in its schema YAML, the explicit setting takes absolute precedence.
  2. Column Naming Heuristics:
  3. Fields matching *customer_id*, *account_number*, *transaction_amount*, *opening_balance* are automatically tagged CONFIDENTIAL.
  4. Fields matching *password*, *secret*, *token*, *api_key* are automatically tagged RESTRICTED.
  5. Model-to-Column Inheritance:
  6. Raw database tables (raw.*) inherit CONFIDENTIAL by default.
  7. Analytical models (analytics.*) inherit INTERNAL by default, with confidential attributes flagged at column level.

docs.title: 1. Overview & Semantic Principles
docs.text:
Financial metrics in the Financial Services Analytics & AI Platform are strictly governed by explicit algebraic definitions, dimensional grains, and currency conversion rules.

LLMs, autonomous agents, and business dashboards are prohibited from inventing ad-hoc formulas or calculating financial totals without adhering to this certified catalogue.

docs.title: Currency Rules:
docs.text:
• Native Currency Aggregation: Multi-currency amounts (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF) must NEVER be summed together without grouping by currency.
  • Reporting Currency Conversion: For cross-currency portfolio comparisons, queries MUST use the explicit _eur reporting columns (e.g. transaction_amount_eur, net_recognized_revenue_eur) which use synthetic daily mid-market FX rates (ECB_SYNTH).
  • Precision: Monetary calculations use numeric(18,4) to prevent IEEE 754 floating-point inaccuracies.

docs.title: Query 1: Monthly Recognized Revenue by Commercial Customer Segment
docs.text:
SELECT
    c.customer_segment,
    r.reporting_month,
    SUM(r.net_recognized_revenue_eur) AS recognized_revenue_eur
FROM analytics.fct_customer_revenue r
JOIN analytics.dim_customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_segment, r.reporting_month
ORDER BY r.reporting_month, recognized_revenue_eur DESC;

docs.title: Query 2: Fee Concessions & Realization Rate by Fee Type
docs.text:
SELECT
    fa.fee_type,
    fa.currency,
    SUM(fa.gross_assessed_amount) AS total_assessed,
    SUM(fa.waived_amount) AS total_waived,
    SUM(fa.collected_amount) AS total_collected,
    ROUND(
        (SUM(fa.collected_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(fa.net_collectible_amount), 0) * 100)::numeric,
        2
    ) AS collection_realization_pct
FROM analytics.fct_fee_assessments fa
GROUP BY fa.fee_type, fa.currency
ORDER BY total_assessed DESC;

docs.title: Governed Financial Metric Catalogue
docs.text:
This catalogue establishes the single source of truth for financial, fee lifecycle, and commercial transaction metrics across the Enterprise AI Analytics Platform.

[!IMPORTANT] Governance Rules 1. Currency Integrity: Native currency amounts (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF) are never summed across different currencies. Multi-currency aggregations must either group by currency or sum the explicitly converted *_eur columns. 2. Fee Lifecycle Separation: Gross assessed fees, waived fees, net collectible fees, collected fees, outstanding arrears, reversed revenue, pass-through costs, and net recognized revenue are distinct financial concepts and must never be treated as interchangeable. 3. AI SQL Boundary: Downstream AI agents and analytical applications must reference these governed definitions and mart models rather than redefining calculations ad hoc.

docs.title: 1. Gross Assessed Fees (MET-01)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Total contractual fees evaluated on eligible settled transactions before applying commercial or tier-based fee waivers.
  • Exact Formula: SUM(gross_assessed_amount) by currency, or SUM(gross_assessed_amount_eur) in EUR reporting currency.
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments (or analytics.fct_customer_revenue).
  • Grain: Assessment level (assessment_id) or monthly customer-category grain (customer_revenue_id).
  • Currency Treatment: Evaluated in the account/transaction native currency (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF). Converted to EUR using the daily ECB_SYNTH mid-rate on assessed_date.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date (or reporting_month).
  • Treatment of Failed/Pending Transactions: Excluded (FAILED and PENDING transactions do not trigger fee assessments).
  • Treatment of Waivers: Included prior to deduction (gross_assessed_amount = waived_amount + net_collectible_amount).
  • Treatment of Partial Collections & Reversals: Unaffected; reflects initial contractual fee calculation.
  • Known Limitations: Synthetic pricing schedules evaluate flat base fees plus basis points in native currency without multi-tier monthly retro-rebates.

docs.title: 2. Waived Fees (MET-02)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Portion of gross assessed fees foregone by the bank due to contractual relationship discounts, promotional waivers, or volume tier concessions.
  • Exact Formula: SUM(waived_amount) by currency, or SUM(waived_amount_eur) in EUR.
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments.
  • Grain: Assessment level (assessment_id).
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency or explicitly converted waived_amount_eur.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date.
  • Treatment of Failed Transactions: Excluded.
  • Treatment of Waivers: Captures both PARTIALLY_WAIVED and WAIVED_IN_FULL assessments.
  • Treatment of Partial Collections & Reversals: Waived fees are never billed or collected.
  • Known Limitations: Waiver reason codes are synthetic descriptors (Commercial relationship tier partial waiver).

docs.title: 3. Net Collectible Fees (MET-03)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Net contractual fee amount due from the customer after deducting commercial waivers from gross assessed fees.
  • Exact Formula: SUM(net_collectible_amount) where net_collectible_amount = gross_assessed_amount - waived_amount.
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments.
  • Grain: Assessment level (assessment_id).
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency or net_collectible_amount_eur.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date.
  • Treatment of Failed Transactions: Excluded.
  • Treatment of Waivers: Net of waivers.
  • Treatment of Partial Collections: Represents the ceiling that collection sweeps may collect (collected_amount + outstanding_amount = net_collectible_amount).
  • Treatment of Reversals: Unchanged by post-collection reversals.
  • Known Limitations: Assumes synchronous assessment at transaction settlement.

docs.title: 4. Collected Fees (MET-04)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Total fee cash successfully swept from customer subledger accounts into bank fee revenue accounts.
  • Exact Formula: SUM(collected_amount) by currency, or SUM(collected_amount_eur) in EUR.
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments (assessment-level roll-up) or analytics.fct_fee_collections (attempt-level grain).
  • Grain: assessment_id or collection_id.
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency or collected_amount_eur.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date (on fct_fee_assessments) or attempted_date / settled_date (on fct_fee_collections).
  • Treatment of Failed Transactions: Excluded.
  • Treatment of Waivers: Waived amounts are excluded before collection targets are set.
  • Treatment of Partial Collections: Includes settled and partial sweep amounts; failed sweeps contribute 0.0000.
  • Treatment of Reversals: Gross collected cash prior to any subsequent revenue reversal.
  • Known Limitations: Collection attempts in the current DEV dataset execute as a single sweep attempt (collection_attempt_number = 1).

docs.title: 5. Outstanding Fees / Uncollected Arrears (MET-05)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Collectible fee balance remaining unpaid after collection sweep attempts fail (e.g., due to INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS or ACCOUNT_FROZEN).
  • Exact Formula: SUM(outstanding_amount) where outstanding_amount = net_collectible_amount - collected_amount.
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments.
  • Grain: assessment_id.
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency or outstanding_amount_eur.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date.
  • Treatment of Failed Collection Attempts: Directly captures operational revenue leakage from failed collection sweeps.
  • Known Limitations: Does not model aging buckets (30/60/90 days past due) or bad-debt write-offs.

docs.title: 6. Reversed Fee Revenue (MET-06)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Previously collected fee revenue refunded or reversed back to the customer.
  • Exact Formula: SUM(reversed_amount) (on fct_fee_assessments) or SUM(reversed_revenue_amount) (on fct_customer_revenue).
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments / analytics.fct_customer_revenue.
  • Grain: assessment_id or customer_revenue_id.
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency or reversed_amount_eur.
  • Date Field Used: assessed_date / recognized_date.
  • Treatment of Reversals: Deducted from gross_collected_revenue when computing net_recognized_revenue.
  • Known Limitations: Synthetic DEV dataset has 0.0000 reversed fee revenue on settled fee collections (while transaction reversals are tested in ledger entries).

docs.title: 7. Net Recognised Revenue (MET-08)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Authoritative bottom-line fee revenue recognised by the bank after deducting fee reversals and direct network/interchange pass-through costs from gross collected fees.
  • Exact Formula: $$\text{Net Recognised Revenue} = \text{Gross Collected Revenue} - \text{Reversed Revenue} - \text{Pass-Through Cost}$$
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_customer_revenue / analytics.fct_fee_assessments.
  • Grain: customer_revenue_id or assessment_id.
  • Currency Treatment: Native currency (net_recognized_revenue) or EUR (net_recognized_revenue_eur).
  • Date Field Used: reporting_month / assessed_date / recognized_date.
  • Treatment of Failed Collections: Failed collection attempts (collection_status = 'FAILED') generate zero recognized revenue.
  • Known Limitations: Uses cash-collection-based revenue recognition rather than IFRS 15 multi-period accrual accounting.

docs.title: 8. Transaction Volume (MET-09), Value (MET-10), and Average Value (MET-11)
docs.text:
• Business Definition: Count, total principal amount, and mean principal amount of commercial transactions, segmented by transaction_status (SETTLED, PENDING, REVERSED, FAILED).
  • Exact Formula:
  • Volume: COUNT(transaction_id)
  • Value (Native): SUM(transaction_amount) grouped by transaction_currency
  • Value (EUR): SUM(transaction_amount_eur)
  • Average Value (EUR): AVG(transaction_amount_eur)
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_transactions.
  • Grain: transaction_id.
  • Currency Treatment: Never sum transaction_amount across currencies; use transaction_amount_eur for cross-currency totals.
  • Date Field Used: transaction_date (initiated_at::date).
  • Treatment of Failed/Pending/Reversed Transactions: Filter on transaction_status = 'SETTLED' for settled commercial volume, or inspect all statuses for operational funnel analysis.

docs.title: 9. Fee Collection Rate (MET-13) and Fee Leakage Indicators (MET-14, MET-15)
docs.text:
• Business Definition:
  • Fee Collection Rate (MET-13): Percentage of net collectible fees successfully swept into cash (SUM(collected_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(net_collectible_amount), 0)).
  • Commercial Waiver Rate (MET-14): Percentage of gross assessed fees conceded via waivers (SUM(waived_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_assessed_amount), 0)).
  • Total Fee Leakage Rate (MET-15): Combined share of gross assessed fees lost to commercial waivers plus operational collection failures (SUM(waived_amount + outstanding_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_assessed_amount), 0)).
  • Source Model: analytics.fct_fee_assessments / analytics.fct_customer_revenue.
  • Currency Treatment: Computed per native currency or using EUR-converted numerator and denominator.
